title: Solving Simultaneous Equations for Both Mean and Standard Deviation

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. Two boundaries 40 and 64 correspond to standard normal scores $z_1 = -1.0$ and $z_2 = 1.0$ respectively. Find $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. The boundaries 30 and 54 have standard normal scores $z_1 = -1.5$ and $z_2 = 1.5$ respectively. Find $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ satisfies $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. It is given that $10 - \mu = -1.282\sigma$ and $24 - \mu = 0.994\sigma$. Find $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: Using the equations from drill 3, $10 - \mu = -1.282\sigma$ and $\sigma = 6.151$, find $\mu$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of $\mu$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The random variable $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ satisfies $\text{P}(X < 30) = 0.20$ and $\text{P}(X < 50) = 0.70$. State the signed $z$-scores corresponding to $X = 30$ and $X = 50$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of $z_1$ and $z_2$ correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.text: The random variable $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ satisfies $\text{P}(X < 45) = 0.20$ and $\text{P}(X > 70) = 0.10$. State the signed $z$-scores corresponding to $X = 45$ and $X = 70$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of $z_1$ and $z_2$ correct to 3 decimal places.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. It is given that $\text{P}(X < 40) = 0.1587$ and $\text{P}(X < 64) = 0.8413$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down two simultaneous equations connecting $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve these equations to find the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

questions.text: The masses $M$ grams of peaches are modelled by a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is found that 10% of peaches weigh less than 120 g and 10% weigh more than 160 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value of the mean $\mu$ by symmetry.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Set up a standardisation equation and find the value of $\sigma$, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The random variable $X$ has a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is given that $\text{P}(X < 30) = 0.20$ and $\text{P}(X < 50) = 0.70$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Formulate two simultaneous equations connecting $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the simultaneous equations to find the value of $\sigma$ and the value of $\mu$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The lengths $X$ cm of timber planks are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is given that $\text{P}(X < 45) = 0.20$ and $\text{P}(X > 70) = 0.10$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Convert the conditions into standard normal equations for $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equations to find $\sigma$ and $\mu$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: In an examination, scores $S$ are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is found that 12% of candidates score more than 75 marks, and 20% of candidates score less than 40 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the standard normal $z$-scores corresponding to 40 marks and 75 marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

questions.text: The battery lifetimes $X$ hours of an electronic sensor are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is found that 30% of batteries last fewer than 36.0 hours, and 15% last longer than 60.0 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the cumulative probability associated with each boundary and obtain the two signed $z$-scores.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Form and solve a pair of simultaneous equations to find the mean lifetime $\mu$ and the standard deviation $\sigma$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Using $\mu = 44.1$ and $\sigma = 15.4$, find the probability that a randomly chosen sensor battery lasts between 40.0 and 55.0 hours.

questions.text: In a quality inspection of 300 manufactured steel rods, the lengths $L$ cm are modelled by a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. Inspection reveals that 36 rods have length less than 40.0 cm, and 24 rods have length greater than 58.0 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Estimate the proportions $\text{P}(L < 40.0)$ and $\text{P}(L > 58.0)$, and find the corresponding standard normal $z$-scores.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence estimate the mean length $\mu$ and the standard deviation $\sigma$, giving both answers to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: In a random sample of 5 rods, find the probability that exactly 1 rod has length less than 40.0 cm, using $\text{P}(L < 40.0) = 0.120$.
